summary: This NVIDIA Isaac AMR documentation page explains how to install and run the Navigation Stack container with the Nova Carter robot in Omniverse Isaac Sim. It covers writing a configuration file, starting the Navigation Stack and waiting for a TCP connection, connecting Isaac Sim via the GXF Bridge extension (manually or via a Python script), and visualizing in Isaac Sight. It also covers AWS deployment, using custom occupancy maps for new environments, and known limitations such as a memory leak in Isaac Sim.
one_line: Guide to running NVIDIA's Isaac AMR Navigation Stack with the Nova Carter robot in Omniverse Isaac Sim, including setup, connection, and custom maps.
key_facts: The Navigation Stack tutorial uses the Nova Carter platform in Omniverse Isaac Sim.
The tutorial's configuration uses lidar-based localization and wheel-inertial odometry, with robot as carter and physics_engine as isaac-sim.
The sample configuration sets linear_speed_limit to 1.111 and omap_cell_size to 0.05.
The Navigation Stack container is run with docker using the --gpus all, --rm and --network=host flags and the -c /tmp/config.yaml argument.
The Navigation Stack initially logs 'Failed to connect to TCP server 127.0.0.1:7000' until Isaac Sim connects.
Isaac Sight is opened in a web browser at http://<ip_address>:3000 and stays blank until the simulation is running.
In Isaac Sight the robot goal is visualized as a red circle, and it can be repositioned by clicking and dragging the marker.
Omniverse Isaac Sim currently supports Isaac AMR in a specific prebuilt Docker image, not its latest release image.
Isaac AMR has only been tested on AWS among cloud platforms, and AWS instances should be g4dn.2xlarge or better (T4) or g5.2xlarge or better (A10G) rather than p2.2xlarge.
Manually running Isaac Sim requires enabling the GXF Bridge extension via Window > Extension and then clicking Play after the Navigation Stack waits for TCP.
Pausing the Isaac Sim simulation also pauses the Navigation Stack, and Destroy Application resets the robot to its initial position.
Stopping the simulation with the Stop button leaves the server running, and clicking Play afterward causes the Navigation Stack to end fatally.
The run_scene.py script in tools/isaac_amr runs Isaac Sim via Python and must be started only after the Navigation Stack is waiting for a TCP connection.
A custom environment requires generating a new occupancy map and setting omap_path and omap_to_world_transform in the configuration file.
A known memory leak occurs in Isaac Sim when the Quick Search and Curve Editor extensions are enabled, with memory possibly growing by 50% over 24 hours.
